## In plain English
A new consumer project's AGENTS.md starts with the line `One-line project description (edit me).`. Gate #4544 stops product work from finishing while that line is still there, and since #5178 the gate also fixes the line itself: it copies the confirmed Overview from PROJECT-DEFINITION into it. Three things go wrong. It copies the whole first line of the Overview, which is often a 700-character paragraph. It does this as a side effect of any agent write (and of `deft check`, occupancy release and `scope:complete`), so an operator who reverts it sees it come back on the next write. And it does it in swarm worker worktrees too, where AGENTS.md is outside the story's file scope, so the worker cannot commit it and it stays as an unexplained dirty file.

## Pains
- P1 — The one-liner is the whole Overview. `oneLinerFromConfirmedOverview` takes the first non-empty line, with no sentence split and no length cap; a one-paragraph Overview becomes a multi-sentence header line, trailing `Source:` text included.
- P2 — The write is a silent side effect and ignores a revert. It runs inside PreToolUse markWrite, inside `deft check` (evaluate calls enforce on a dirty tree), occupancy release and `scope:complete`. Nothing tells the operator, and a reverted header is rewritten on the next hooked write.
- P3 — Worker worktrees get the write. The hook runs on the worktree root, so a swarm worker's checkout gets an AGENTS.md change outside its story `file_scope`; the fence and the commit scope-cover gate refuse it, and it is rewritten after each restore.

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- #6914: the general class of process-owned files that the fence refuses (deft-checkpoint). This arc may say what the header write needs from the fence, but does not build a general admission.
- Setup Phase 3 itself (`content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md`, owned by the installer/setup owner). This arc keeps to the header write path.
- The #4544 refusal itself (placeholder plus product work, no Overview): kept unless a critic shows it must change.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/platform/agents-consumer-header.ts` 28-35 `oneLinerFromConfirmedOverview` (first non-empty line, heading marks stripped, nothing else); 89-121 `compareAndSetConsumerHeaderOneLiner` (placeholder-only CAS); 209-269 `evaluateFirstShipHeaderPlaceholderGate` (placeholder plus product-mutation refuses; absent, custom and Process-only pass).
- `packages/core/src/check/consumer-header-placeholder.ts` 322-326 `readConfirmedOverviewAtRoot`; 329-388 `evaluateConsumerHeaderPlaceholderAtRoot`, which at 373-382 calls the enforce path (a write) when the tree has dirty product paths and no marker; 419-633 `enforceConsumerHeaderPlaceholderAtCompletionChokepoint` (stamps `.deft/cache/product-mutation-completion.json`, reads Overview 488-493, CAS 534-537, re-read guard 542-571, write 572); 639-660 `enforceConsumerHeaderPlaceholderWhenProductEvidence`.
- `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` 4060-4077: markWrite with `persistProductMutationMarker` runs the chokepoint before the lease publish and fails the write on refuse; 2318 the markWrite flag; 2697 occupancy release runs the evidence wrapper.
- `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 2886-2903: PreToolUse re-check passes `persistProductMutationMarker` on product allows, rooted at `effectiveRoot` (a worker's worktree root).
- `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` 838 and 926: `scope:complete` runs the evidence wrapper.
- `packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.ts` 185: `deft check` calls the evaluate path (and so the write at 373-382).
- `packages/core/src/session/main-worktree.ts` 32: `isLinkedWorktreePath` exists.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` 801: setup names the placeholder-only CAS from user-confirmed Overview; no verb performs it, so the chokepoint is the only production writer.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. Derivation. `oneLinerFromConfirmedOverview` returns the first sentence of the first non-empty line, cut at a word boundary to a fixed cap held in its own named constant (about 120 characters), with a trailing `Source:` clause dropped. A one-sentence Overview line is unchanged.
- R2. Linked worktrees. When the project root is a linked worktree, the chokepoint neither writes AGENTS.md nor refuses on the placeholder; it passes with a reason that names the primary checkout. The first-ship refusal stays on the primary checkout.
- R3. Decline. When the chokepoint writes the header it records the line it wrote in an ignored path (`.deft/cache/consumer-header-oneliner.json`). If the header is the placeholder again while that record exists, the operator reverted it: the chokepoint does not write again and treats the header as a Process-only choice (pass, with a message naming how to set the line by hand).
- R4. Report. Every write prints one line naming the file and the new one-liner (hook warning channel, `check` output, `scope:complete` output).
- R5. Evaluate does not write. `evaluateConsumerHeaderPlaceholderAtRoot` (the `deft check` / verify path) evaluates only; the write stays in the markWrite and `scope:complete` chokepoints.
- R6. Moving the write out of markWrite into a named verb is split to a follow-up unless the critics show the lean cannot bind without it.
- R7. Tests: a multi-sentence one-paragraph Overview gives one capped sentence; a reverted header is not rewritten; a linked worktree gets no write and no refusal; `deft check` on a dirty tree writes nothing; a reproduction of the reported sequence (Overview of several sentences, product write, header filled with the full paragraph) fails before the fix.

Questions for the critics:
1. Does R1 give a usable one-liner for real Overviews (abbreviations such as "e.g.", a first sentence longer than the cap, Markdown, a leading heading)? Should the cap truncate or should the write refuse and ask?
2. R2: if a linked worktree skips the refusal, can first-ship product work finish without the gate ever firing (a worker's `scope:complete` in its worktree, a repo that only uses worktrees)? What should the worktree do instead?
3. R3: is "placeholder again after we wrote" a sound decline signal? What about a fresh clone, a deleted cache, a second operator, or a placeholder restored by a merge? Does treating a decline as a pass reopen the #4544 class?
4. AC 2 of the issue asks that the write not run as a side effect of an ordinary write. Can the lean bind with R1-R5 and the verb split out (R6), or must the write move now? If it moves, what makes the gate's refusal still reachable and fixable?
5. AC 3 asks that the change be committable. With R2 and R3, where does the header change land and who commits it? Is a fence admission needed here, or is it #6914's?
6. Does any part add a new gate, refusal, constant or network read? Name each. What is the smallest buildable slice?

## In plain English

R1–R7 cannot bind as written. They improve the description’s length, but retain the automatic write that the issue explicitly asks to remove. They also leave primary-checkout changes outside the story’s permitted files. Skipping checks in worktrees and interpreting a restored placeholder as consent would let product work bypass the existing first-ship rule. The smallest coherent fix is an explicit, scoped header operation, with existing completion checks remaining read-only.

## Answers to the six questions

1. **R1 needs a defined fallback.** A leading `# Overview` becomes “Overview”; punctuation splitting can break “e.g.”; truncation can produce an incomplete sentence. Offer a capped candidate and accept an operator-confirmed one-liner when extraction is ambiguous. Do not introduce a new refusal on ordinary writes. “One-sentence Overview unchanged” must be qualified when it exceeds the cap.

2. **Yes, R2 can bypass first-ship enforcement.** Worktree topology does not establish that another checkout will run the gate. Suppress automatic header writes everywhere; retain read-only evaluation in workers. Resolve the header in an authorized primary-checkout change and bring that committed change into workers. Never redirect a worker’s write into the primary checkout.

3. **No, R3 is not a sound consent signal.** A merge, reset, branch switch, or another operator can restore the placeholder. Cache deletion reverses the supposed decision. Existing Process-only means no product evidence; it does not mean product work with a declined header. Removing automatic writes makes a decline cache unnecessary for preventing rewrites.

4. **The write must move now.** R5 addresses only one caller, while R6 explicitly postpones AC2. Keep the existing product-evidence checks reachable, but replace their automatic remediation with a runnable named remedy. The current remedy names an internal function rather than a CLI operation.

5. **R2 and R3 provide no landing path.** The primary checkout still needs scope coverage. Prefer a small, explicit lifecycle change whose governing scope includes `AGENTS.md`. A narrow admission is an alternative, but must cover both the write fence and staged commit checks; a general #6914 solution is unnecessary.

6. **Additions:** R1 adds a cap constant; R3 adds a cache record and an authorization-like exemption; R2 adds a topology exemption. R4 adds reporting; R5 removes writes. No network read or new refusal is inherently required. The smallest slice is: remove implicit header writes, add one explicit scoped operation with placeholder-only CAS and output, preserve read-only checks, and test all implicit callers plus commit coverage. ## Summary

The AGENTS.md header completion chokepoint pastes the whole Overview narrative into the one-liner, on any agent write, outside every story file_scope

## Context

Directive 0.130.2 and 0.131.0 consumer, Claude Code host hooks, Phase 2 narratives confirmed via setup:seed --answers and project:write-narratives (Overview is about 700 characters, several sentences). The unmanaged AGENTS.md header still had the scaffold line One-line project description (edit me). Source: internal benchmark evidence (private).

## Expected behavior

The header write fills a one-line description (one sentence, or a short summary the operator confirms), not the full Overview narrative. It happens as an explicit, operator-visible step (setup Phase 3 or a named verb), and the change lands in a commit the agent is allowed to make: either AGENTS.md is admitted by the scope fence for this write, or the verb opens its own small lifecycle change.

## Actual behavior / gap

enforceConsumerHeaderPlaceholderAtCompletionChokepoint (check/consumer-header-placeholder.js, #4544 / #5178 / #5253) runs from session/occupancy.js on markWrite with persistProductMutationMarker and from scope/transition.js on scope:complete. On an ordinary agent Edit of RESULTS.md it stamped .deft/cache/product-mutation-completion.json (recordedAt matches the edit) and silently rewrote the AGENTS.md one-liner with the entire Overview narrative (multi-sentence, with a Source: path). The change is uncommitted. The write fence then refuses AGENTS.md as outside the active story file_scope, and the commit scope-cover gate refuses it too, so the agent cannot land it and it stays dirty. Discarding it with git restore only lasts until the next hooked write, which rewrites it again. This repeated in three sessions, including once in a swarm worker worktree, where it showed up as an unexplained uncommitted change.

## Session notes

Acceptance: (1) the header write derives a single-line description (first sentence or an operator-confirmed one-liner), never the full multi-sentence Overview; (2) it is not triggered as a side effect of an ordinary Write/Edit or occupancy markWrite: it runs at setup Phase 3 or through a named verb, and reports what it wrote; (3) the resulting AGENTS.md change is committable without fighting the scope fence (fence admits it for this write, or the verb opens its own lifecycle PR); (4) an operator who reverts the header is not overwritten again on the next write (respect a declined or Process-only choice); (5) a worker worktree never gets this write. Related: deftai/directive#4544 (closed; origin of the gate), #6914 (same class: process-owned files refused by the fence).
